Details of bee processing: Forager worker bees collect pollen from flowers, moisten it with regurgitated nectar/honey, and add salivary glandular secretions. Pollen is not consumed by bees in this form.
Sampling method: Collected from pollen traps attached to the hive entrance that detach pellets from the pollen baskets on bee legs.

Details of bee processing: Pollen foragers deposit collected pollen into hive cells before younger in-hive worker bees process and pack the collected pollen, adding honey and glandular secretions. Stored pollen has a dry and powdery appearance. It can be consumed by nurse bees in this form, though their preference is for bee bread.
Sampling method: Collected from the brood frame within the hive. Stored pollen age varies but was taken before significant fermentation had occurred (typically within 1–2 days of packing).

Details of bee processing: Formed from stored pollen after anaerobic lactic fermentation by Lactobacillus. Bee bread has awet and sticky appearance. It is consumed by nurse bees and fed to larvae mostly in the form of jelly.
Sampling method: Collected from the brood frame within the hive. Bee bread age is from a few days up to 3 weeks following collection by bees from flowers.
